# T13a quartz (crates/quartz): A and C extensions (RV64IMAC)
Worker: hydrogen-high. First read `briefs/_RULES.md`, then `crates/quartz/src/inst.rs`,
`inst/decode.rs`, `exec.rs`, `csr.rs`, `trap.rs` (the existing RV64IM hart; keep its style).
The official riscv-tests (T13) come later; this task uses LLVM as the oracle.

**May touch:** `crates/quartz/**` except `tests/fixtures/` (leader data, do not edit).
`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, `no_std` + `alloc`, zero external crates. All existing tests keep passing.

## Why
rustc's riscv64gc output (compressed code and atomics) must run on Quartz: the Rust kernel
(T25), the assembler (T21) and the hypervisor (T31) need it.

## API additions (exact)
```rust
// quartz::inst
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AmoOp { Swap, Add, Xor, And, Or, Min, Max, Minu, Maxu }
// new Inst variants (aq, rl are the ordering bits; decode and encode them):
LrW { rd: u8, rs1: u8, aq: bool, rl: bool },  LrD { rd: u8, rs1: u8, aq: bool, rl: bool },
ScW { rd: u8, rs1: u8, rs2: u8, aq: bool, rl: bool },  ScD { /* same */ },
AmoW { op: AmoOp, rd: u8, rs1: u8, rs2: u8, aq: bool, rl: bool },  AmoD { /* same */ },
/// Expand a 16-bit compressed instruction to the `Inst` of its 32-bit equivalent
/// (c.addi rd, i -> Addi { rd, rs1: rd, imm: i }, c.mv rd, rs2 -> Add { rd, rs1: 0, rs2 }, ...).
/// None for reserved encodings, FP forms and halfwords whose low two bits are 11.
pub fn decode_c(h: u16) -> Option<Inst>;
```
`encode` handles the new variants (32-bit forms only; no compressed encoder needed).
`decode` of an LR with rs2 != 0 is None.

## C extension (RV64C, spec "C" chapter)
- Quadrants 00/01/10: C.ADDI4SPN C.LW C.LD C.SW C.SD C.NOP C.ADDI C.ADDIW C.LI C.ADDI16SP C.LUI
  C.SRLI C.SRAI C.ANDI C.SUB C.XOR C.OR C.AND C.SUBW C.ADDW C.J C.BEQZ C.BNEZ C.SLLI C.LWSP
  C.LDSP C.JR C.MV C.EBREAK C.JALR C.ADD C.SWSP C.SDSP. Expansions exactly as the spec table
  (C.BEQZ rs1' -> Beq { rs1, rs2: 0, imm }, C.JR -> Jalr { rd: 0, rs1, imm: 0 }, C.JALR ->
  Jalr { rd: 1, .. }, C.LI -> Addi { rs1: 0 }, C.NOP -> Addi { 0, 0, 0 }, C.EBREAK -> Ebreak).
- None: all-zero halfword, C.ADDI4SPN with nzuimm 0, C.LWSP/C.LDSP with rd 0, C.JR with rs1 0,
  C.ADDI16SP with imm 0, C.LUI with imm 0, C.ADDIW with rd 0, quadrant 00 funct3 100, and the FP
  forms C.FLD C.FSD C.FLDSP C.FSDSP (no F/D here). HINT encodings (e.g. C.LI with rd 0) may decode.
- Execution: a compressed instruction advances pc by 2; C.JALR links pc + 2. IALIGN becomes 16:
  jumps and taken branches to a target that is 2 mod 4 are legal; only an odd target is
  misaligned (JALR already clears bit 0). `xepc` writes clear only bit 0.
- Fetch: read 16 bits; if the low two bits are 11 read the next 16 bits too. If the second half
  faults (access or page fault), the trap value is the address of that second half and pc stays
  at the instruction start. An illegal compressed instruction traps with the halfword as tval.
- `misa` gains A (bit 0) and C (bit 2).

## A extension (RV64A)
- AMO*.W/D: load the old value (W: sign-extend the 32-bit value) into rd, store op(old, rs2)
  (W ops work on 32 bits; MIN/MAX signed, MINU/MAXU unsigned; W leaves the upper half of the
  doubleword alone). One read and one write through the bus; also on MMIO.
- LR.W/D loads (W sign-extends) and sets a reservation on that address. SC.W/D succeeds only if
  the reservation is valid and for the same address: stores rs2, rd = 0; otherwise rd = 1 and no
  store. Every SC (success or not) clears the reservation; taking any trap clears it.
- Faults: address not a multiple of the access size -> AMO/SC `StoreMisaligned(addr)` (cause 6),
  LR `LoadMisaligned(addr)` (cause 4). Bus faults: AMO/SC -> `StoreFault`, LR -> `LoadFault`; page
  faults: AMO/SC -> store page fault (15), LR -> load page fault (13). An AMO needs a page that is
  readable and writable (D bit set like a store).
- aq/rl change nothing on this single hart.

## Tests required
Table tests per compressed form and per AMO op (W and D, sign cases), LR/SC sequences, misaligned
and faulting accesses, a 32-bit instruction straddling the end of memory, a jump to 2 mod 4,
mixed 2- and 4-byte programs run on `Machine`, `forall` round trips (decode(encode(i)) == i for
random new variants), and fuzz: `decode_c` of every u16 never panics.

## Extra check the leader will run
`crates/quartz/tests/ac_leader.rs`: 2500 compressed halfwords from LLVM 19 against the word LLVM
gives for the expanded instruction; 1200 A-extension words (decode and encode); a compressed
self-checking program and an atomics self-checking program on `Machine`; a rustc-built
riscv64gc Rust program (sorting, atomics, u128 division, core::fmt) that must print the same
hash the host computes; 4000 random AMOs against a reference model; LR/SC and fault table.
